title: Add support for .mdc files under .clinerules/ directory
body:
### Description

## Overview

This PR adds support for loading `.mdc` files (Markdown files with metadata) within the `.clinerules` directory. This enables dynamically applying relevant instructions only when requests match specific file patterns.

## Background and Necessity

Previously, the `.clinerules` directory supported only simple text-based rule files. As projects grow in scale, there's an increasing demand for more flexible and detailed rule specifications.

Inspired by Cursor's Project Rule functionality, we've introduced Markdown-based metadata to manage rules more flexibly. This provides the following benefits:

- Rules can be conditionally applied using glob patterns.
- Metadata such as titles and descriptions improve readability and management.

## Implementation Details

When `.mdc` files are present in the `.clinerules` directory, the processing follows these steps:

1. Match file paths specified in the latest request against glob patterns defined in the `.mdc` files.
2. Only when matched, load the `.mdc` file content and return it along with metadata (title and description).

## Example

Usage Example

Below is a practical example of an .mdc file:

backend-guidelines.mdc

```md
---
title: Backend Development Guidelines
description: Rules for writing backend code
glob: "backend/**/*.js"
---

## Coding Rules

- All functions must use async/await syntax.
- Use camelCase for variable naming.
- Remove unnecessary console.log statements.
- API responses must include HTTP status codes.
- Load environment variables from a .env file.
- Limit function arguments to five or fewer.
- Use shared modules for database connection handling.
- Implement detailed error handling with try-catch blocks.
- Add comments only to complex code sections.
- Immediately remove unused code.
```

The above .mdc file applies only to requests targeting JavaScript files within the backend/ directory.

## Additional Notes

- If a parsing error occurs, the original file content is returned to maintain usability.
- Existing text-based rule files continue to function as before.

title: Remove Delay Package
body: ### Description - Replaced the delay package with Node.js built-in setTimeout from node:timers/promises. This removes an external dependency and prevents ESM/CommonJS compatibility issues that causes intermittent test failures. **The change is recommended by the delay package authors themselves** and provides identical functionality with no external dependencies. - The issue relates to module system incompatibility. The delay package (v6.0.0+) is a pure ESM module, while our test configuration (tsconfig.test.json) compiles to CommonJS. This causes errors when test files try to require() an ESM-only module. The error message showed: `Error [ERR_REQUIRE_ESM]: require() of ES Module /node_modules/delay/index.js not supported.` This is an intermittent issue - I noticed the tests worked again after running npm install:all. This is likely due to either: - Node module resolution caching behavior - Dependency tree restructuring affecting how modules are resolved - Specific test execution order avoiding the problematic code paths However, the fundamental incompatibility still exists and could resurface in different environments or CI pipelines. Replacing delay with native setTimeout from node:timers/promises permanently fixes the ESM/CommonJS conflict. ### Test Procedure Ensured that the tests were running. Ensured that delays are still working as expected, for example when getting usage data from Openrouter. ### Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] 📚 Documentation update ### Pre-flight Checklist - [x] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs) - [x] Tests are passing (`npm test`) and code is formatted and linted (`npm run format && npm run lint`) - [x] I have created a changeset using `npm run changeset` (required for user-facing changes) - [x] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) ### Screenshots ### Additional Notes ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Replaced `delay` package with Node.js's `setTimeoutPromise` to fix ESM/CommonJS compatibility issues and remove an external dependency. > > - **Dependency Removal**: > - Removed `delay` package from `package.json`. > - **Code Changes**: > - Replaced `delay` with `setTimeoutPromise` from `node:timers/promises` in `.clinerules`, `openrouter.ts`, `Cline.ts`, `ClineProvider.ts`, `extension.ts`, `BrowserSession.ts`, and `McpHub.ts`. > - Ensures identical functionality with native `setTimeoutPromise`. > - **Issue Fix**: > - Resolves ESM/CommonJS compatibility issues causing intermittent test failures. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=cline%2Fcline&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for 362025d8ec849d5f46c19318530f5e97b7dbcae5. title: ContextManager Tests
body: ### Description This PR adds comprehensive tests for the `ContextManager` module, which is responsible for context window management in Cline. These tests verify the correct functionality of the `getNextTruncationRange` and `getTruncatedMessages` methods that handle conversation truncation when approaching context limits. The tests cover a range of scenarios: - First-time truncation with both "half" and "quarter" keep strategies - Sequential truncation (multiple truncations over time) - Proper handling of the alternating user-assistant message pattern - Edge cases like small message arrays - Verification that the message structure remains intact after truncation ### Test Procedure - All tests were verified to pass using `npm run test` ### Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] 📚 Documentation update ### Pre-flight Checklist - [x] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs) - [x] Tests are passing (`npm test`) and code is formatted and linted (`npm run format && npm run lint`) - [x] I have created a changeset using `npm run changeset` (required for user-facing changes) - [x] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) ### Screenshots ### Additional Notes ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Add tests for `ContextManager` truncation methods in `ContextManager.test.ts`. > > - **Tests Added**: > - `getNextTruncationRange` tests in `ContextManager.test.ts` for first and sequential truncations with half and quarter keeps, ensuring correct truncation ranges and message roles. > - `getTruncatedMessages` tests in `ContextManager.test.ts` for handling no range, specific range removal, and maintaining message alternation pattern. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=cline%2Fcline&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for da3da07f1e1bead6a44105a72a5fab15fbcf2390. [x] the gear icon on the browser embed should just open the settings page and scroll to the relevant area | https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/2439 - [x] pre-load chrome executable path with our best guess, so user doesn't feel like they *need* to fill it in - [x] add telemetry with task ID Cleanup / Nice To Have -- - [x] use or delete old comments from Saoud - [x] double check all the message passing flows between Cline.ts/ClineProvider.ts - [x] if the site requests to send notifications that will generate a pop up. Prevent popups? - [x] Test with WSL - [x] Test loading of old conversations Known Issues -- - [x] re-loading a task where we have a remote browser connection doesn't always load the previously cached image, especially with this web notifications test site https://www.bennish.net/web-notifications.html - [x] check that re-launching works consistently, it seems to refuse when its already in debug mode? - [x] remove advanced settings configs from package.json & check basic settings still work - [x] fix headless mode | https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/2451 - [x] Weird behaviour: `chromeLauncher.killAll()` fails to kill my existing Chrome & then the new instance launched doesn't detect my existing profiles. This opens a way to launch a separate Chrome w/ debugging without killing the old one, which is interesting. Maybe there's something bugged on my computer, it needs more testing. The stated goal is to have it open with your existing chrome profile(s). Launching chrome manually in debug mode works. Ah, the reason from the documentation is that killAll() is for killing sessions we launched, not any session running on the system: https://github.com/GoogleChrome/chrome-launcher#readme | another issue is perhaps the sandboxing mechanics: https://github.com/puppeteer/puppeteer/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md - [x] when vscode is quit, the chrome session that we started as a sub-process gets rudely crashed. We don't transition the user back to what they had before they interacted with Cline. We should at least gracefully shut down Chrome so that it can restore state correctly on the next run - [x] fix prompt not being updated when browser settings update - [x] Transitioning between remote -> local mode within a single task isn't being respected, stays remote ---- De-scoped for future PRs -- - [x] some kind of UI for which style of browser connection we're doing | https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/2453 | **de-scoped because we need non-context metadata storage about what kind of browser was used in the past** - [ ] in thinking mode, json blobs of browser actions frequently in output - [ ] Figure out how to remove the advanced settings chrome executable path UI. `vscode.workspace.getConfiguration().update('myExtension.mySetting', undefined, true);` https://code.visualstudio.com/api/references/vscode-api#WorkspaceConfiguration - [ ] Cline *always* installs chromium in the first run. We actually now detect the binary path robustly, so we should prefer to use the user's existing chrome. Installing chromium should be shown in UI and cancelable - [ ] UI for downloading chromium progress / cancel - [ ] have to re-launch chrome to achieve transitions between headless/non-headless mode - [ ] enable browser for all models that do image use - [ ] if there's no fresh tab on open (or outside of a tab group), cline doesn't close the tab it opened - [ ] sometimes sites open new tabs, and we don't track them or force it into one tab. title: Fix for headless browser option
body: ### Description This change corrects an issue with the headless option in the browser feature. For local browser launches with Puppeteer, we changed to use the newer Puppeteer v23+ method which requires 'shell' instead of 'true' for the more performant headless implementation. title: Feat: automatic retry for Gemini 2.5 Pro 503 Server Busy error (#2471)
body: ### Description This PR introduces an automatic retry mechanism for API calls made to Gemini models (specifically targeting Gemini 2.5 Pro, but potentially applicable to others) when the API responds with a 503 "Server Busy" status code. Currently, these transient errors interrupt the workflow and require manual intervention. This change implements a respectful retry strategy within `src/core/Cline.ts` to handle these specific 503 errors automatically, improving the reliability and user experience when interacting with Gemini. Modifications were also made to `src/shared/ExtensionMessage.ts`, `src/shared/WebviewMessage.ts`, and `webview-ui/src/components/chat/ChatRow.tsx`. The retry mechanism is invisible to the user. ### Test Procedure Used it in prod all day I am confident that this change will not introduce bugs because the retry logic is specifically scoped to 503 errors in general and also those with the specific wording used by Gemini 503 responses. Existing error handling for other statuses remains unchanged. ### Type of Change - [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] 📚 Documentation update ### Pre-flight Checklist - [x] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs) - [x] Tests are passing (`npm test`) and code is formatted and linted (`npm run format && npm run lint`) - [x] I have created a changeset using `npm run changeset` (required for user-facing changes) - [x] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) ### Screenshots No UI changes. ### Additional Notes Considered adding configuration options for retry behavior but opted for a default implementation first. ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Adds automatic retry mechanism for Gemini 2.5 Pro API calls on 503 errors, with retry logic implemented in `Cline.ts` and `ChatRow.tsx`. > > - **Behavior**: > - Adds automatic retry for Gemini 2.5 Pro API calls on 503 errors in `Cline.ts`. > - Retry logic in `ChatRow.tsx` triggers on specific error messages ("503 Service Unavailable" or "model is overloaded"). > - Retries are delayed randomly between 3-7 seconds. > - **Message Handling**: > - Adds `retryApiRequest` type to `ExtensionMessage` and `WebviewMessage`. > - Implements retry logic in `ClineProvider.ts` for handling `retryApiRequest` messages. > - **Misc**: > - Removes incorrect import for `getRandomInt` in `Cline.ts` and defines it locally in `ChatRow.tsx`. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=cline%2Fcline&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for 433c9498506b1e154e0c4f321fde09c99b93d0b9. body: ----- **Note from me** This is my first ever GitHub contribution and I've only been coding for about 6 months, so I'm open to any feedback or suggestions for improvement. Future enhancements will extend support to other external MCP tools beyond Claude Desktop - I'm excited to contribute this feature as I believe it creates a valuable workflow for users who want to leverage both Cline and Claude Desktop -------------------------------- This PR introduces two key features that enable seamless integration between Cline and external MCP tools like Claude Desktop: - Active Conversation Marking: Users can mark conversations as "Active A" or "Active B", allowing external MCP tools to detect and access these conversations. - Notification System Bridge: External MCP tools can send messages, suggestions, and advice to active Cline conversations through the notification system. **This creates a cost-effective workflow where users can:** - Use Claude Desktop for research and planning (with its $20/month subscription) - Send targeted advice and solutions to Cline through the notification system - Leverage Cline's powerful code editing capabilities without incurring per-message costs for research and planning - Test Procedure I've manually tested these features by: - Verifying notification creation and display - Testing notification interaction (read, dismiss, restore, send to chat) - Testing active conversation toggling - Verifying integration with Claude Desktop via the cline-mcp-tools server - Testing edge cases (e.g., no active task, multiple extension instances) - All tests passed successfully and the features work as expected. ## MCP Tools Installation To use this feature, users need to install the cline-mcp-tools MCP server: ### Prerequisites - Node.js 18.0.0 or higher - Claude Desktop application - **IMPORTANT**: The forked version of the Cline VS Code extension from: https://github.com/anthonyjj89/cline-mcp-external-link (this one) ### Download and Build 1. title: Add coverage tests to github workflow for PRs to `main`
body: ### Description This PR adds test coverage validation to our CI/CD process. It ensures that new code doesn't degrade our test coverage by comparing coverage metrics between the base branch and the PR branch. Also fixes major bug preventing extension tests from being run: ``` 1) Extension Tests should activate extension successfully: Activating extension 'saoudrizwan.claude-dev' failed: Cannot find module '/home/runner/work/cline/cline/dist/extension.js' ``` Key improvements: - Added a coverage job to the GitHub workflow that runs after the test job - Configured the test job to run tests with coverage and save the results using workflow-scoped artifacts - Implemented coverage comparison between base branch and PR branch - Added PR comments with coverage metrics and warnings when coverage decreases - Optimized the workflow to avoid running tests twice and prevent artifact bloat - Added unit tests to ensure proper function of the coverage workflow - Added extension build step to ensure extension tests properly run Note: It is dependent on the prior PR: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/2499 ### Test Procedure - Install [uv](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv#installation) and [act](https://nektosact.com/installation/homebrew.html) if you don't have them - `cd .github/scripts && uv venv .venv && uv pip install requests && source .venv/bin/activate && python3 tests/coverage_check_test.py -v` ### Type of Change - [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - It implements a GitHub workflow that uses these scripts to validate coverage between branches. The workflow is designed to be non-blocking - it will warn about coverage decreases but won't fail the PR. This encourages developers to maintain or improve test coverage without blocking critical changes. Key features of the implementation: 1. **Efficient test execution**: Tests with coverage are run in the test job, and the results are passed to the coverage job 2. **No artifact bloat**: Using `retention-period: workflow` ensures artifacts are automatically deleted when the workflow completes 3. **Different coverage formats**: The workflow handles both the main extension tests and webview-ui tests, which have different coverage output formats 4. **Non-blocking validation**: The workflow warns about coverage decreases but won't fail the PR ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow to validate test coverage in PRs to `main`, compares coverage metrics, and posts results, while fixing a bug in extension tests. > > - **GitHub Actions Workflow**: > - Adds a coverage job to `test.yml` that runs after the test job. > - Compares coverage metrics between base and PR branches. > - Posts PR comments with coverage metrics and warnings if coverage decreases. > - Optimizes workflow to avoid running tests twice and prevent artifact bloat. > - **Bug Fix**: > - Fixes bug preventing extension tests from running due to missing `extension.js`. > - **Scripts and Utilities**: > - Adds `coverage_check` package with modules for extraction, comparison, and GitHub API interactions. > - Implements CLI in `__main__.py` for coverage extraction and comparison. > - Adds unit tests in `coverage_check_test.py` for coverage utilities. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=cline%2Fcline&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for 1e28d3bd3db3ba4921f02ae80ebe78411ad62100. title: Updated feedback to model when diff edit fails
body: ### Description Everyone experiences Cline messing up a targeted search & replace edit and then immediately jumping to write an entire file. This is pretty painful to watch, and leaves a bad taste in your mouth. In my experience working with cline, telling him to "Please re-read the contents of the entire file, then make a proper, TARGETED search & replace diff edit" works every time, and gets me back on track. So I'd like to 1. Include these instructions that I usually type manually in the automated diff_error feedback the model gets. 2. Bias cline towards being more persistent with the tool. Imo, trying to use is almost ALWAYS a mistake after a failed . I am aware we already send `this.diffViewProvider.originalContent` -- but clearly it's not enough if my manual instructions to re-read the file and make a proper search and replace diff edit consistently works to get Cline back on track. I'm torn between removing that altogether and just asking cline to re-read, or keeping it, and asking cline to re-read on top of having `originalContent`, as an opportunity for cline to read, take a breather, and think about what a proper targeted diff edit should look like. ### Test Procedure ### Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] 📚 Documentation update ### Pre-flight Checklist - [ ] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs) - [ ] Tests are passing (`npm test`) and code is formatted and linted (`npm run format && npm run lint`) - [ ] I have created a changeset using `npm run changeset` (required for user-facing changes) - [ ] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) ### Screenshots ### Additional Notes ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Improves feedback for failed search and replace operations in `Cline.ts` to encourage re-reading files and retrying targeted edits. > > - **Behavior**: > - Updates feedback in `Cline.ts` for failed search and replace operations to instruct re-reading the file and retrying a targeted edit. > - Suggests using `replace_in_file` over `write_to_file` to avoid unnecessary full file writes. > - **Misc**: > - Adds a changeset file `breezy-items-bake.md` for version tracking. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=cline%2Fcline&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for d366ff3744f2f63024e52e64f93615b66f94d146. title: Fix matching errors in the blockAnchorFallbackMatch method of diff.ts caused by using some special line matching in extreme cases; for example, using '/**' as the starting line and '}' as the ending line.
body: ### Description #2544 In the blockAnchorFallbackMatch method, when a block is matched using the first and last lines; 1. If only one block is matched; then calculate the average similarity and pass if it exceeds 0.5; otherwise, consider the match as failed 2. If multiple blocks are matched, sort them based on average similarity and select the highest one; if the similarity exceeds 0.7, it passes; otherwise, it is considered a failed match. ### Test Procedure ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4482826d-3cdb-40be-a799-f30ccc9616ed) ### Type of Change - [X] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] 📚 Documentation update ### Pre-flight Checklist - [X] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs) - [X] Tests are passing (`npm test`) and code is formatted and linted (`npm run format && npm run lint`) - [X] I have created a changeset using `npm run changeset` (required for user-facing changes) - [X] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) ### Screenshots ### Additional Notes If time allows; please take a look at another [PR 2334](https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/2334); this issue has been around for some time, the following SEARCH-REPLACE block causes the 'replace_in_file' tool to perform incorrect replacements; resulting in the need for manual edits to the diff editor content. If you have any better suggestions for a fix or follow-up plans, please let me know. ``` <<< SEARCH content ======= new content >>>>>>> REPLACE ``` ``` <<<<<<< SEARCH content ======= new content ``` ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Improves `blockAnchorFallbackMatch` in `diff.ts` with Levenshtein-based similarity checks for better block matching, adding tests in `diff_edge_cases3.test.ts`. > > - **Behavior**: > - `blockAnchorFallbackMatch` in `diff.ts` now uses Levenshtein distance to calculate similarity for block matching. > - If one block matches, it passes if similarity > 0.5; if multiple, the highest similarity > 0.7 is chosen. > - **Functions**: > - Adds `levenshtein()` function in `diff.ts` for calculating string similarity. > - **Tests**: > - Adds `diff_edge_cases3.test.ts` to test new matching logic with cases of single and multiple block matches. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=cline%2Fcline&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for 6c8f21ea30600b7194caf8573add571246379e2e. title: feat(mention): Add support for @note
body: ### Description #### Overview: The @note feature allows users to save notes within relevant files by adding content following the @note: tag in the text. This feature simplifies the process of adding annotations to code or documents for later reference. The note's save location is automatically determined as either the .clinerules file or the .clinerules/clinenotes.md file. #### Target The note's save location is automatically determined based on the presence of the .clinerules directory. If the .clinerules directory exists, the note is saved to the .clinerules/clinenotes.md file. If the .clinerules directory does not exist, the note is saved to the .clinerules file. The note format is Markdown. #### Assignment - Is @note a good name for the feature? This is debatable. - Is “:” OK for separator? I was also worried about using a blank space, but I decided to use this method because it is better to record and continue the process, as in “@note:something Please continue development.” - Name of .clinerules/clinenotes.md. title: feat: support of workspace level MCP servers
body: ### Description # Feature: Local Project MCP Server Configuration & Chat UI Integration ## Problem Solved Currently, all MCP (Model Context Protocol) server configurations are managed globally through a single settings file (`cline_mcp_settings.json`). This approach lacks flexibility for project-specific needs and requires navigating away from the chat interface to manage or check server status. Users cannot easily: * Define servers that are only relevant to a specific project/workspace. * Override global server configurations (e.g., change environment variables or arguments) for a particular project without affecting others. * Keep project-related server configurations version-controlled alongside the project code. * Quickly view server status or manage servers directly from the chat input area. ## Solution Implemented This Pull Request introduces support for project-level MCP server configurations using a `.cline_mcp_servers.json` file in the project root. It also adds a dedicated MCP status button and popup directly within the chat text area for quick access and management. ## Key Changes 1. **Local Configuration File Support:** * The system now looks for a `.cline_mcp_servers.json` file in the root of the active workspace. * Added `WorkspaceFileNames.mcpServers` constant in `src/core/storage/disk.ts`. 2. **Configuration Merging:** * Implemented logic within `src/services/mcp/McpHub.ts` (`loadAndMergeMcpSettings`) to read both the global `cline_mcp_settings.json` and the local `.cline_mcp_servers.json`. * Server configurations are merged into a single list used by the application. * **Local Override:** If a server name exists in both files, the configuration from the local `.cline_mcp_servers.json` takes precedence. 3. **Server Source Tracking:** * Added an optional `source` property (`'global'` or `'project'`) to the `McpServer` type definition in `src/shared/mcp.ts` using constants `MCP_SOURCE_GLOBAL` and `MCP_SOURCE_PROJECT`. * The `McpHub` tracks the origin of each active server configuration. 4. **Enhanced File Watching:** * The `McpHub` now watches both global and local settings files for changes, triggering reloads. 5. **Context-Aware Settings Modification:** * Functions within `McpHub` (e.g., `toggleServerDisabled`, `deleteServer`) now automatically determine and modify the correct settings file (global or project) based on the server's source. 6. **UI Updates & New Features:** * **Chat MCP Button & Popup:** Added a new MCP status icon button (`codicon-server-process`) in the `ChatTextArea.tsx` controls, next to the model selector. Clicking this button opens a popup (`McpServerStatusPopup.tsx`) displaying the status of all configured servers (global and project), allowing users to quickly enable/disable, restart servers, and open configuration files without leaving the chat context. * **Source Indicator:** Added a visual indicator (`(global)` or `(project)`) next to each server name in the MCP Hub "Installed" tab (`McpView.tsx`) and the new chat popup (`McpServerRow.tsx`). Tooltips explain the source file. * **Configuration Buttons:** Replaced the single "Configure MCP Servers" button in `McpView.tsx` and added distinct "Global Config" / "Local Config" buttons to `McpServerStatusPopup.tsx` for easier access to the respective settings files. The "Local Config" button creates the file if it doesn't exist. * **Message Handling:** Added the `openLocalMcpSettings` message type and handler. This feature significantly enhances the flexibility and usability of MCP servers by allowing project-specific configurations and providing convenient in-chat status checking and management. ### Test Procedure What has been tested: - title: Fixing the UX bug for Requestly Provider's  model selection
body:
### Description Solves the issue https://github.com/cline/cline/issues/2536 where Requesty API shows the same default model claude sonnet 3.7 in model selection.
Explanation ## Core problem: The normalizeApiConfiguration function at the bottom of ApiOptions.tsx is responsible for figuring out the selectedProvider, selectedModelId, and selectedModelInfo based on your settings. It has specific case blocks for providers like "anthropic", "bedrock", "openrouter", etc., but was missing a case for "requesty": block. ## Fallback Behavior: Because there's no specific case for "requesty", the code falls through to the default: case at the end. The default case uses the settings for the "anthropic" provider (anthropicModels and anthropicDefaultModelId). Result: This means that whenever "requesty" is selected as the provider, the UI incorrectly uses Anthropic's default model ID (which is likely claude-3-7-sonnet-20240715) and its corresponding info, leading to "Claude 3.7 Sonnet" always being displayed, even though the backend (RequestyHandler) is was using the correct requestyModelId you entered(I verified in the UX) ## Solution: I added a specific case "requesty": block within the switch (provider) statement in the normalizeApiConfiguration function in webview-ui/src/components/settings/ApiOptions.tsx. This new case will correctly retrieve the requestyModelId from the apiConfiguration and use the right model info.

title: eng-332/Diff editing context management
body: ### Description This PR introduces a file tracking metadata system to Cline that enhances diff edit reliability. The system logs which files Cline reads, edits, or creates during a task and actively monitors them for user modifications. If a tracked file is changed by the user, Cline is proactively notified in subsequent API requests via environment details, prompting it to re-read the file before making edits. This prevents stale content issues and significantly reduces diff edit failures. The implementation includes a FileContextTracker for interaction logging and modification detection, and a structured task_metadata.json to persist file states across sessions. This tracking mechanism improves the accuracy, reliability, and resilience of Cline’s diff editing capabilities. ### Test Procedure Introduce the full contents of one or more file into the context by: - Mentioning the file - Having Cline read the file - Having Cline create the file - Having Cline modify the file Complete or cancel the task, then edit one of these files. Resume the task, instructing Cline to edit one of these files. It should read the file before starting the edit. These changes can be confirmed by viewing api_conversation_historyjson (in globalStorage/saoudrizwan.claude-dev/tasks) and locating the following text in : `These files have been modified since Cline last accessed them (file was just edited so you may need to re-read it before editing):\n` task_metadata.json (same location) should contain the file tracking metadata. title: Fix/duplicate bom
body: ### Description Fixes a bug in `DiffViewProvider` where editing a file with a Byte Order Mark (BOM) could result in a duplicate BOM being inserted into the document buffer during the streaming update process. The issue occurred because: 1. Incoming content (`accumulatedContent`) contained a BOM when the original file has BOM. 2. `vscode.workspace.applyEdit`, when replacing content from the start of the file (0,0), might also implicitly preserve or add a BOM based on the original file's state. This combination led to two BOMs (`\ufeff\ufeff`) appearing at the beginning of the buffer. The fix involves unconditionally stripping any leading BOM from the `accumulatedContent` within the `update` method *before* it is passed to `applyEdit`. This prevents the duplication, relying on `applyEdit` and the later `saveChanges` method to correctly handle the final BOM state based on the original file's requirements. **Related Issues:** * Fixes #947 * Fixes #2463 ### Test Procedure The issue was identified and debugged through interactive testing and analysis of the `applyEdit` behavior with BOM files. **Steps to reproduce the bug (before fix) and verify the fix:** 1. Create a file named `temp.txt` with the following content: ``` a b c ``` 2. In VS Code, change the file encoding to "UTF-8 with BOM". (Click on the encoding in the status bar, select "Save with Encoding", choose "UTF-8 with BOM"). 3. Ask Cline to perform an edit, for example: "replace c with d in temp.txt". **Expected behavior:** * **Before fix:** During the streaming update in the diff view, a duplicate BOM (`\ufeff\ufeff`) might appear at the beginning of the file content in the editor buffer. The final saved file might also contain issues depending on subsequent save logic. * **After fix:** The streaming update proceeds without inserting a duplicate BOM. The final saved file correctly contains only a single BOM. Manual testing confirmed that editing a BOM file no longer results in duplicate BOMs in the editor buffer during streaming updates, and the final saved file correctly retains the single BOM. ### Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] 📚 Documentation update ### Pre-flight Checklist - [x] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs) - [x] Tests are passing (`npm test`) and code is formatted and linted (`npm run format && npm run lint`) - [x] I have created a changeset using `npm run changeset` (required for user-facing changes) - [x] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) ### Screenshots N/A ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Fixes duplicate BOM issue in `DiffViewProvider` by stripping BOM from `accumulatedContent` in `update()` method. > > - **Bug Fix**: > - In `DiffViewProvider`, `update()` method now strips leading BOM from `accumulatedContent` to prevent duplicate BOMs during streaming updates. > - Relies on `applyEdit` and `saveChanges` to handle BOM based on original file state. > - **Related Issues**: > - Fixes #947 > - Fixes #2463 > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=cline%2Fcline&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for 943a190f6b7b66012d5ebb6732b0cdabaeeaf0a2. title: fix: respect chromeExecutablePath setting in UrlContentFetcher
body: ### Description This PR fixes issue #2510 where the "@http://" command was failing to use the custom chrome executable path specified in settings, while the "Visit" command worked fine. The root cause was that `BrowserSession.ts` (used by the "Visit" command) properly checked for and respected the `cline.chromeExecutablePath` configuration setting, while `UrlContentFetcher.ts` (used by the "@http://" command) did not include this check. This change modifies the `ensureChromiumExists()` method in `UrlContentFetcher.ts` to mirror the same logic used in `BrowserSession.ts`, ensuring both commands use the same approach to determine the Chrome executable path. ### Test Procedure 1. Configure a custom Chrome executable path in VSCode settings with `cline.chromeExecutablePath` 2. Test the "Visit https://www.example.com" command to verify it works as expected 3. Test the "@http://www.example.com" command to verify it now uses the same executable path 4. Confirm the browser launches correctly in both cases This change is minimal and only affects how the Chrome executable path is determined, mirroring existing well-tested logic from `BrowserSession.ts`. The fix doesn't modify any browser behavior or arguments, so it should not introduce new bugs. ### Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] 📚 Documentation update ### Pre-flight Checklist - [x] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs) - [x] Tests are passing (`npm test`) and code is formatted and linted (`npm run format && npm run lint`) - [x] I have created a changeset using `npm run changeset` (required for user-facing changes) - [x] I have reviewed [[contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) ### Screenshots N/A ### Additional Notes This change essentially ports the Chrome executable path detection logic from `BrowserSession.ts` to `UrlContentFetcher.ts` to ensure consistent behavior across both browser-related features. title: feat: drag and drop files and folders into chat
body: ### Description This PR introduces the ability for users to drag and drop files and folders directly from the VS Code explorer into the Cline chat input area. - When dropping a file/folder, you have to hold shift and drop into the text area - When items are dropped, their workspace-relative paths are inserted into the input as `@` mentions (e.g., `@/src/file.ts`, `@/src/folder/`). - Dropped folders automatically receive a trailing slash in their path mention. - Supports dropping multiple files and/or folders simultaneously. - The implementation correctly handles the different data types provided by VS Code during drag-and-drop (`resourceurls` for multi-item drops, `application/vnd.code.uri-list` as a fallback). - Uses a state queue (`pendingInsertions`) and a `useEffect` hook to insert multiple paths sequentially, ensuring correct state updates and cursor positioning between insertions. - Ensures that existing drop functionalities (plain text, images) remain operational and correctly prioritized. ### Test Procedure 1. **Single File:** Drag a single file from the VS Code explorer into the chat input. Verify its relative path is inserted correctly as a mention (e.g., `@/path/to/file.ext `). 2. **Single Folder:** Drag a single folder. Verify its relative path is inserted with a trailing slash (e.g., `@/path/to/folder/ `). 3. **Multiple Files:** Drag multiple files. Verify all paths are inserted, separated by spaces (e.g., `@/file1.ts @/file2.js `). 4. **Multiple Folders:** Drag multiple folders. Verify all paths are inserted with trailing slashes and spaces (e.g., `@/folder1/ @/folder2/ `). 5. **Mixed Items:** Drag a mix of files and folders. Verify all paths are inserted correctly with appropriate trailing slashes for folders. 6. **Plain Text:** Drag selected plain text from another application or editor into the chat input. Verify the text is inserted directly at the cursor position. 7. **Image File:** Drag an image file (e.g., PNG, JPG) from the file system (not VS Code explorer) into the chat input. Verify the image is added as an attachment preview below the input area. Confidence: High. The implementation specifically addresses the data types observed during testing (`resourceurls`) and maintains the correct priority order for different drop types (VS Code resources > Images > Plain Text). The queue system handles sequential insertions reliably. ### Type of Change - [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] 📚 Documentation update ### Pre-flight Checklist - [x] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs) - **Behavior**: > - Enables drag-and-drop of files/folders into chat input, inserting workspace-relative paths as `@` mentions (e.g., `@/src/file.ts`). > - Supports multiple files/folders, adding trailing slashes for folders. > - title: Enhance ollama provider
body: ### Description This PR enhances the Ollama provider to match the robustness of the OpenAI provider. The Ollama provider currently lacks several important features that the OpenAI provider has, leading to issues like the infinite "thinking" problem while when run on command like with ollama run, it is responsive. Key improvements: 1. **Added Retry Mechanism**: Implemented the `@withRetry()` decorator to automatically retry failed requests with exponential backoff. 2. **Timeout Handling**: Added timeout handling using Promise.race to prevent infinite "thinking" when Ollama doesn't respond. 3. **Enhanced Error Handling**: Added comprehensive try/catch blocks with detailed error reporting. 4. **Improved Stream Processing**: Enhanced the stream processing to handle token usage metrics and properly propagate stream errors. 5. **Comprehensive Tests**: Created thorough tests that verify all the new functionality. 6. **Optional Tests**: Made tests skip automatically when Ollama is not running locally, improving CI reliability. These changes should significantly improve the reliability of Ollama models in Cline, particularly resolving the infinite "thinking" problem that users frequently experience. ### Test Procedure - Added comprehensive unit tests for the Ollama provider that verify: - Successful responses - Timeout handling - Retry mechanism - Stream processing errors - All tests are passing with `npm run test:unit -- src/api/providers/__tests__/ollama.test.ts` - Tests automatically skip if Ollama is not running locally - Manually tested with Ollama running locally to verify that timeouts and retries work as expected (requires running `ollama run llama2` command externally first) ### Type of Change - [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] 📚 Documentation update ### Pre-flight Checklist - [x] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs) - [x] Tests are passing (`npm test`) and code is formatted and linted (`npm run format && npm run lint`) - [x] I have created a changeset using `npm run changeset` (required for user-facing changes) - [x] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) ### Screenshots N/A ### Additional Notes This PR addresses a common issue reported by users where Ollama models get stuck in a "thinking" state indefinitely. The changes bring the Ollama provider up to the same level of robustness as the OpenAI provider, despite Ollama offering OpenAI-compatible endpoints. ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Enhance Ollama provider with retry, timeout, and error handling, and add comprehensive tests for improved reliability. > > - **Enhancements to `OllamaHandler` in `ollama.ts`:** > - Added `@withRetry()` decorator to `createMessage()` for automatic retries on errors. > - Implemented timeout handling using `Promise.race` to prevent infinite waiting. > - Improved error handling with detailed logging and error messages. > - Enhanced stream processing to handle token usage metrics and propagate stream errors. > - **Testing in `ollama.test.ts`:** > - Added tests for successful responses, timeout handling, retry mechanism, and stream processing errors. > - Tests skip if Ollama is not running locally, improving CI reliability. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=cline%2Fcline&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for 5aa0b3e82150976d0cb08d0e7941db13e04dbaa0. title: Replace Anthropic Bedrock SDK with native AWS Bedrock Runtime SDK
body: ### Description This PR replaces the dependency on `@anthropic-ai/bedrock-sdk` with the native AWS Bedrock Runtime SDK (`@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime`) for all Anthropic model calls through Bedrock. This aligns with how other models like DeepSeek and Nova are already implemented, providing a more consistent approach across all Bedrock models and reducing external dependencies. By using the native AWS Bedrock Runtime SDK directly, we gain several important benefits: 1. **Access to Bedrock Guardrails** - Direct integration with AWS Bedrock's content filtering and safety features 2. **Unified API through Converse API** - Simplified handling of different models through a standardized interface, making future model additions much easier 3. **Enhanced AWS integration** - Better compatibility with AWS authentication mechanisms and credential providers 4. **Simplified dependency management** - Reduced external dependencies and consistent versioning with other AWS services 5. **Future-proofing** - Better positioned to adopt new Bedrock features like knowledge bases and model evaluation tools The implementation maintains all existing functionality including streaming responses, token usage tracking, reasoning capabilities, image handling, and error handling, while providing a cleaner path for future enhancements. ### Test Procedure - Tested with Claude 3 Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku models - Verified streaming responses work correctly - Verified token usage tracking works correctly - Verified reasoning/thinking capabilities work correctly - Verified image handling works correctly - Verified error handling works correctly - Ran the full test suite to ensure no regressions ### Type of Change - [] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - Expected XML Output: ``` docs/empty-example.mdFile is empty ``` Note: Shows the self-closing tag and the specific for empty files. #### Example 3: Error reading a non-existent file Scenario: Attempting to read src/nonexistent-component.tsx. Expected XML Output: ``` src/nonexistent-component.tsxFile not found: /Users/pash/Documents/Melden/cline/src/nonexistent-component.tsx ``` Note: Illustrates the error format, omitting the tag and including the specific error message within tags. The exact path in the error message will depend on the user's system. #### Example 4: Error reading a file that's too large (based on current extractTextFromFile limit) Scenario: Attempting to read assets/large-log-file.log which exceeds the size limit (e.g., > 300KB). title: fix (workspace tracker): Replace the workspace events with a FileSystemWatcher
body: ### Description This is a fix for #1340. Following @albemala's [idea](https://github.com/cline/cline/issues/1340#issuecomment-2788491117), I am replacing the workspace events used in the `WorkspaceTracker` with a `FileSystemWatcher` which reacts to any events within the workspace instead of only user actions. The `FileSystemWatcher` is somewhat particular, so I am using `ignore` to ignore the files not returned by `listItems`. I want to use the `ClineIgnoreController` but it requires reorganizing things a bit, so I preferred to limit this PR and follow up with the replacement. ### Test Procedure I added integration tests for the changes. I also tested the changes locally, creating files using a `node` and `bash`, and making sure the webview got the updates. If you want to change these changes by yourself, you can run the extension locally and play around with the mentions menu while modifying files outside of VSCode. For example: 1. `mkdir test` 2. title: bugfix: AWS credentials overridden by env variables in shell init scripts
body: ### Description If a user is setting the `AWS_PROFILE` environment variable in a shell init script (~/.zshrc, ~/.bashrc, etc.) then this profile will always be used instead of any Cline settings. This is due to two factors: 1. `AWS_PROFILE` will always be used over `AWS_ACCESS_KEY` pairs by the AWS SDK. See additional notes for more details. 2. The `AWS_PROFILE` environment variable is only set temporarily when the credential provider is invoked. After, it is restored to the value it was previously. To reproduce, add `export AWS_PROFILE="fake-aws-profile"` to your shell init script. Reload VS Code, use Bedrock authentication, and all API requests will fail. ### Test Procedure 1. `AWS_PROFILE` set to non-existent profile name in ~/.zshrc 2. AWS Profile set to `bedrock` in Cline 3. API calls succeed ### Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor Changes - [ ] 💅 Cosmetic Changes - [ ] 📚 Documentation update - [ ] 🏃 Workflow Changes ### Pre-flight Checklist - [x] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs) - [x] Tests are passing (`npm test`) and code is formatted and linted (`npm run format && npm run lint`) - [x] I have created a changeset using `npm run changeset` (required for user-facing changes) - [x] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) ### Screenshots Error message when `AWS_PROFILE` is set to an account without Bedrock access via shell init script: ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fe0b4118-c163-4c4a-87f0-545e38376b6b) ### Additional Notes There is debug output that describes the AWS SDK behavior regarding prioritization of `AWS_PROFILE`: ``` @aws-sdk/credential-provider-node - defaultProvider::fromEnv WARNING: Multiple credential sources detected: Both AWS_PROFILE and the pair AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY static credentials are set. This SDK will proceed with the AWS_PROFILE value. However, a future version may change this behavior to prefer the ENV static credentials. Please ensure that your environment only sets either the AWS_PROFILE or the AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY pair. ``` I don't see an open issue for this, but internally we have seen multiple users with this issue, and it seems it was mentioned here: https://github.com/cline/cline/issues/852#issuecomment-2627567364 ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Prevents shell-initialized `AWS_PROFILE` from overriding Cline's AWS credential settings in `AwsBedrockHandler.getAwsCredentials()`. > > - **Bugfix (AWS credentials):** > - In `AwsBedrockHandler.getAwsCredentials()` in `bedrock.ts`, deletes `process.env["AWS_PROFILE"]` if `awsUseProfile` is set and `AWS_PROFILE` is present, preventing shell-initialized `AWS_PROFILE` from overriding Cline's AWS credential settings. > - Ensures AWS SDK uses credentials/profile as configured in Cline, not from shell environment variables. > - **Release notes:** > - Adds changeset documenting the fix for AWS_PROFILE override issue. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=cline%2Fcline&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for 23f0e7c1df62eda3d009c59ff1919392f70b0f10. title: Pirate Mode Activated
body: # Add Toggle Functionality to ClineRules ### Description This PR implements toggle functionality for `.clinerules` files and directories. It allows users to selectively enable or disable specific rule files in both global and workspace-specific rule collections, giving users more control over which rules are applied during Cline sessions. Key changes: - Added a new `ClineRulesToggles` type to track enabled/disabled state of rule files - Implemented state persistence for toggles in both global and workspace settings - Added synchronization logic to keep toggle state in sync with actual files - Updated rule processing to respect toggle state - Improved directory reading to filter out hidden files This enhancement provides users with more flexibility when using `.clinerules`, especially when they might want to temporarily disable certain rules without deleting the files. ### Test Procedure I've thoroughly tested this change with the following test cases: #### Directory-based Rules 1. **Global Rules Directory**: Created multiple rule files in the global `.clinerules` directory and verified all are loaded with default enabled state 2. **Local Rules Directory**: Created a project with multiple rule files in a local `.clinerules` directory and confirmed they all load properly 3. **Nested Directories**: Tested with nested subdirectories inside `.clinerules` and verified that all files at any depth are properly found and tracked 4. **Adding Files**: Added new files to the `.clinerules` directory and verified they are automatically detected and enabled 5. **Removing Files**: Removed files from the `.clinerules` directory and confirmed their toggles are properly removed from state 6. **Hidden Files**: Verified that `.DS_Store` and other hidden files are correctly identified and excluded from rule processing #### File-based Rules 6. **Local Rules File**: Tested with a single `.clinerules` file (not a directory) and verified it loads properly #### Transition Cases 8. **Directory to File Transition**: Changed a `.clinerules` directory to a single file and verified toggle state is properly updated 9. **File to Directory Transition**: Changed a single `.clinerules` file to a directory with multiple files and confirmed toggle state is synchronized #### Persistence & Separation 10. **State Persistence**: Verified toggle states persist across VSCode sessions All tests confirm that the toggle functionality works correctly, with proper synchronization when file structure changes and proper state persistence. title: Improve AWS region selection strategy to avoid "429 Too many tokens, please wait before trying again."
body: ### Description This is the implementation for https://github.com/cline/cline/discussions/2188 The idea is to allow users to choose multiple AWS regions as potential inference endpoints to avoid 429 errors due to quota limits. The new implementation will use this list of Regions to cycle around every time it gets a 429 from the AWS region currently in use, allowing the process to keep moving forward without manually having to retry the calls or change regions. This is implemented as an extension of the current `@withRetry({ maxRetries: 3, regionCycling: true })` allowing other providers that could support the functionality to also implement it. ### Test Procedure Run a full end to end test on a dev vscode environment with massive improvement on user experience for low quota limit users. title: Compile src and test files when running tests on CI
body: ### Description Recently, the `pretest` script was failing because of an import. It was fixed [here](https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/2910/files#diff-38fe7260aba3d97b269c965701427c72ff19017e2eb8fad3a38b3a23cb015d36), but I suspect it was missed on CI because `compile` is used on CI, which results in only one of the integration tests running: --- Now that tests run, they fail because they can't resolve paths. You can check the [workflow](https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/2930/checks), but this is the output: ``` Error: Cannot find module '@utils/cost' Require stack: - /home/runner/work/cline/cline/out/utils/cost.test.js - /home/runner/work/cline/cline/node_modules/mocha/lib/mocha.js - /home/runner/work/cline/cline/node_modules/mocha/index.js - /home/runner/work/cline/cline/node_modules/@vscode/test-cli/out/runner.cjs - /home/runner/work/cline/cline/.vscode-test/vscode-linux-x64-1.99.3/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/api/node/extensionHostProcess.js ``` I will open a follow-up PR to fix this issue. ### Test Procedure To verify the issue: 1. Clear your `out` directory. 2. Run `npm run compile` 3. Run `npm run test:integration` 4. See how many specs run. You can run `pretest` and `test:integration`, go to the test workflow output, or see above to verify the PR. title: Use context length from lite llm
body: ### Description When liteLLM is used as LLM provider, "sane defaults" are used for context window length. This is laudable of course, but may be severely limiting if liteLLM also proxies models with very large context windows like the new Gemini models or the newest OpenAI models, which support up to 1M tokens. This PR introduces changes to query liteLLM for the model options, and hence supported context length, of the model currently in use. Since this is not known before the model is actually selected, this is done asynchronically. ### Test Procedure I've run the modified Cline extension for some example chats, the context length was updated correctly. ### Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - title: ENG-501/Detection of command termination using Ctrl+C

title: refactor: Make reasoning effort setting model independent
body: ### Description Refactors the `o3MiniReasoningEffort` setting and related logic to be model-independent. Previously, this setting was specifically tied to OpenAI's o3-mini model, but the functionality was also being used for other o3/o4 models and in the OpenRouter and Requesty providers. This change generalizes the concept of a 'reasoning effort' setting and allows it to be applied to any model that supports this feature by adding a `supportsReasoningEffort` flag to the `ModelInfo`. Modified files: - `package.json`: Renamed the configuration setting key from `cline.modelSettings.o3Mini.reasoningEffort` to `cline.modelSettings.reasoningEffort` and updated the description. - `src/shared/api.ts`: Renamed `o3MiniReasoningEffort` to `reasoningEffort` in `ApiHandlerOptions` and added `supportsReasoningEffort?: boolean` to the `ModelInfo` interface. Updated `openAiNativeModels` and `xaiModels` to set `supportsReasoningEffort: true` for relevant models. - `src/api/providers/openai.ts`: Updated to use `this.options.reasoningEffort` and check `model.info.supportsReasoningEffort`. - `src/api/providers/cline.ts`: Updated to pass `this.options.reasoningEffort` to `createOpenRouterStream`. - `src/api/providers/openai-native.ts`: Updated to use `this.options.reasoningEffort` and check `model.info.supportsReasoningEffort`. - `src/api/providers/requesty.ts`: Updated to use `this.options.reasoningEffort` and check `model.info.supportsReasoningEffort`. - `src/api/transform/openrouter-stream.ts`: Renamed the `o3MiniReasoningEffort` parameter to `reasoningEffort` and updated the logic to check `model.info.supportsReasoningEffort`. - `src/core/storage/state.ts`: Updated to read the `cline.modelSettings.reasoningEffort` configuration setting. - `webview-ui/src/components/settings/ApiOptions.tsx`: Updated the UI logic to use `selectedModelInfo.supportsReasoningEffing effort control. ### Test Procedure 1. Verified that the project builds without TypeScript or linting errors. 2. Checked the Settings UI to confirm that the 'Modify reasoning effort' checkbox and dropdown appear only when a model that supports reasoning effort (e.g., OpenAI Native o3/o4-mini, XAI Grok 3 mini) is selected. 3. title: Fix: Expand ${workspaceFolder} for MCP stdio transport cwd/env
body: ### Description This PR addresses an issue where the `${workspaceFolder}` variable was not being expanded when used in the `cwd` (current working directory) or `env` (environment variables) fields for MCP servers configured with the `stdio` transport type, particularly when using the global Cline settings file. **Problem:** - Servers launched via Cline would start in an incorrect directory (e.g., the VS Code installation directory) instead of the intended project workspace root specified by `${workspaceFolder}` in the `cwd` setting. - Environment variables defined using `${workspaceFolder}` (e.g., `PROJECT_ROOT`) would contain the literal string `${workspaceFolder}` instead of the resolved path. - This prevented servers from correctly resolving relative file paths based on the active workspace, leading to errors when accessing project files or writing output. **Cause:** The logic within `src/services/mcp/McpHub.ts` for initializing the `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/stdio.js` `StdioClientTransport` did not explicitly handle the expansion of the `${workspaceFolder}` variable for the `cwd` and `env` configuration options before spawning the server process. **Solution:** This PR modifies the `connectToServer` method in `src/services/mcp/McpHub.ts` to: 1. Reliably determine the `workspaceRoot` path using the `vscode.workspace.workspaceFolders` API. 2. Implement an `expand` function that replaces occurrences of the literal string `${workspaceFolder}` with the determined `workspaceRoot`. 3. Apply this `expand` function to the `command`, `args`, `env` values, and the `cwd` value obtained from the server configuration *before* constructing the `StdioClientTransport`. 4. Provide a fallback for `cwd` to default to the determined `workspaceRoot` if `cwd` is not explicitly set in the server configuration. This ensures that the server process is launched with the correct working directory and properly resolved environment variable paths when `${workspaceFolder}` is used in the configuration. ### Test Procedure 1. Configured an MCP server (e.g., `FileDump`) using the `stdio` transport in `cline_mcp_settings.json` (tested with global storage settings). 2. Set `"cwd": "${workspaceFolder}"` in the server configuration. 3. Set `"env": { "PROJECT_ROOT": "${workspaceFolder}" }` in the server configuration. 4. Added debug logging at the start of the target server script (`file_dump_server.py`) to print `os.getcwd()` and `os.getenv('PROJECT_ROOT')`. 5. Launched VS Code in a specific project workspace (e.g., `C:/ArunApps/Chess-Web`). 6. Started the configured MCP server via the Cline interface. 7. **Verified:** Checked the MCP server's output logs. title: Fix: Expand ${workspaceFolder} for MCP stdio transport cwd/env
body: ### Description This PR addresses an issue where the `${workspaceFolder}` variable was not being expanded when used in the `cwd` (current working directory) or `env` (environment variables) fields for MCP servers configured with the `stdio` transport type. **Problem:** - Servers launched via Cline would start in an incorrect directory (e.g., the VS Code installation directory) instead of the intended project workspace root specified by `${workspaceFolder}` in the `cwd` setting. - Environment variables defined using `${workspaceFolder}` (e.g., `PROJECT_ROOT`) would contain the literal string `${workspaceFolder}` instead of the resolved path. - This prevented servers from correctly resolving relative file paths based on the active workspace, leading to errors when accessing project files or writing output. **Cause:** The logic within `src/services/mcp/McpHub.ts` for initializing the `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/stdio.js` `StdioClientTransport` did not include logic to explicitly expand the `${workspaceFolder}` variable for the `cwd` and `env` configuration options (as well as `command` and `args`) before spawning the server process. **Solution:** This PR modifies the `connectToServer` method in `src/services/mcp/McpHub.ts` to: 1. Reliably determine the `workspaceRoot` path using the `vscode.workspace.workspaceFolders` API. 2. Implement an `expand` function that replaces occurrences of the literal string `${workspaceFolder}` with the actual `workspaceRoot` path. 3. Apply this `expand` function to the `command`, `args`, `env` values, and the `cwd` value obtained from the server configuration *before* constructing the `StdioClientTransport`. 4. Provide a fallback for `cwd` to default to the determined `workspaceRoot` if `cwd` is not explicitly set in the server configuration. This ensures that the server process is launched with the correct working directory and properly resolved environment variable paths when `${workspaceFolder}` is used in the configuration. ### Test Procedure 1. Configured an MCP server (e.g., `FileDump`) using the `stdio` transport in settings (e.g., `cline_mcp_settings.json` or workspace `.vscode/settings.json`). 2. Set `"cwd": "${workspaceFolder}"` in the server configuration. 3. Set `"env": { "PROJECT_ROOT": "${workspaceFolder}" }` in the server configuration. 4. Added debug logging at the start of the target server script (e.g., in Python using `os.getcwd()` and `os.getenv('PROJECT_ROOT')`) to print the CWD and relevant environment variable on startup. 5. Launched VS Code in a specific project workspace. 6. Started the configured MCP server via the Cline interface. 7. **Verified:** Checked the MCP server's output logs. Confirmed that the logged `cwd` and the value of the `PROJECT_ROOT` environment variable correctly reflected the actual workspace path, not the VS Code installation directory or the literal string `${workspaceFolder}`. 8. **Verified:** Confirmed that tool calls involving relative paths now correctly resolved paths relative to the workspace root. ### Type of Change - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Documentation update - [ ] Other (please describe): ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Fixes `${workspaceFolder}` expansion issue in MCP stdio transport configurations in `McpHub.ts`. > > - **Behavior**: > - Fixes issue where `${workspaceFolder}` was not expanded in `cwd` and `env` for MCP servers using `stdio` transport in `McpHub.ts`. > - Adds fallback for `cwd` to default to `workspaceRoot` if not set. > - **Implementation**: > - Adds `expand` function in `connectToServer` to replace `${workspaceFolder}` with actual path. > - Applies `expand` to `command`, `args`, `env`, and `cwd` before constructing `StdioClientTransport`. > - **Misc**: > - Updates version to `3.13.1` in `package.json`. > - Updates `CHANGELOG.md` for version `3.13.1`. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=cline%2Fcline&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for 907a43ebfd82fdf68bd9d27b954d6120257f1a14. title: ENG-464 Fix Settings state issue with API provider reseting other settings.
body: ### Description When setting "Use different models for Plan and Act modes" then changing the provider (possibly other settings) for the modes, it will revert the checkbox and state of the settings view. This happens if you start with separate or not. Here is how it happens: 1. handleInputChange updates the local React state for apiProvider. 2. It immediately sends an "apiConfiguration" message to the core extension. The payload is based on the current local React state. 3. This local state might not reflect changes to other settings yet, or might still hold values related to the previous provider. 4. The core extension's updateApiConfiguration function (in src/core/storage/state.ts) receives this potentially incomplete/stale object. 5. Because updateApiConfiguration overwrites all API state keys based only on the received object, any fields missing from the message payload are effectively set to undefined in the persistent storage. 6. The core extension sends this modified state back to the webview. 7. The webview re-renders with the corrupted state, causing the UI elements (like the "Use different models" checkbox, model selections, etc.) to revert or display incorrectly. ### My solution The challenge is that the API provider needs to support instant set for the roll up menu under the chatbox but it also needs to wait and only be set when the user hits done in the settings page. My solution is to support both options For the settings menu we rely on the react state and only update the core state when you hit done for the roll up menue we set it instantly like before preserving the original behavior ### Test Procedure Test the rollup provider menu 1. switch to openrouter or cline provider 2. modify the favorite model 3. set the provider to something else 4. make sure the settings are saved and the favorite are saved Test the settings menu 1. Do the same test as above 2. change the use different models for plan and act 3. change the provider after (this would have caused the bug) 4. hit done to save the provider. ### Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor Changes - [ ] 💅 Cosmetic Changes - [ ] 📚 Documentation update - [ ] 🏃 Workflow Changes ### Pre-flight Checklist - [x] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs) - [x] Tests are passing (`npm test`) and code is formatted and linted (`npm run format && npm run lint`) - [x] I have created a changeset using `npm run changeset` (required for user-facing changes) - [X] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) ### Screenshots ### Additional Notes ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Fixes settings reset bug by ensuring API provider changes are saved only on confirmation, using `saveImmediately` prop for control. > > - **Behavior**: > - Fixes bug where changing API provider resets other settings by ensuring settings are saved only when confirmed. > - Introduces `saveImmediately` prop in `ApiOptions` to control immediate saving of settings. > - **Components**: > - Updates `ApiOptions` to use `saveImmediately` for immediate saving when changing providers. > - Modifies `ChatTextArea` to set `saveImmediately` to `true` for instant saving in popups. > - Changes `SettingsView` to save settings only on confirmation, not on every change. > - **Misc**: > - Renames "Done" button to "Save" in `SettingsView` for clarity. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=cline%2Fcline&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for 873a0b507edd688bc23e91e4ed4ee07fbf3c279b. title: Prevent file editing tools in PLAN mode
body: Copied from -> https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/2141 NOTE: Making a separate PR was easier than overwriting the original PR but once this is merged I will give them credit. ### Description(copied from the PR) This PR prevents file editing tools (`write_to_file` and `replace_in_file`) from being used in PLAN mode. I understand that PLAN mode is intended for information gathering and planning purposes, while actual execution like file editing should be done in ACT mode. This is because PLAN mode is specifically designed for "planning" as opposed to "acting" in ACT mode, with clear role separation between the two. In the current implementation, file editing tools can still be used in PLAN mode, which is inconsistent with the mode's intended purpose. I noticed this issue, and after seeing that other users had mentioned similar concerns in #1621 #2024, I decided to implement this fix. This PR adds the necessary checks to enforce this restriction and updates the system prompt to explicitly state this limitation, ensuring that the system behavior matches the intended purpose of PLAN mode. ### Test Procedure I tested this by: 1. title: Add symlink support for readDirectory
body: ### Description **Issue** Since **v3.13.0**, the **Cline Rules pop‑over** does not load rule files delivered through **symbolic links**. `readDirectory()` was skipping entries where `Dirent.isSymbolicLink()` is `true`, so the pop‑over could not discover those rules. **Fix** * Update `src/utils/fs.ts` so that `readDirectory()` * Detects symlinks, resolves them with `fs.readlink()`, and inspects the target stats. * Returns symlinked files and recursively traverses symlinked directories. * Add comprehensive unit tests in `src/utils/fs.test.ts`. * Add a changeset describing the bug‑fix. ### Test Procedure 1. `npm test` — new test cases cover: * Standard directory traversal. * Symlink → file. * Symlink → directory (recursive). * Graceful failure on missing directories. 2. Manual QA: run Cline with a rules folder containing symlinks and confirm the pop‑over lists them. 3. Regression: verify circular symlinks are safely ignored and performance remains unaffected. ### Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor Changes - [ ] 💅 Cosmetic Changes - [ ] 📚 Documentation update - [ ] 🏃 Workflow Changes ### Pre-flight Checklist - [x] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs) - [x] Tests are passing (`npm test`) and code is formatted and linted (`npm run format && npm run lint`) - [x] I have created a changeset using `npm run changeset` (required for user-facing changes) - [x] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) ### Screenshots _N/A_ ### Additional Notes * **Performance impact:** minimal — traversal is still depth‑first and filters OS artefacts before symlink resolution. * **Edge cases:** circular symlinks are not followed, preventing infinite loops. ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Add symlink support to `readDirectory()` in `fs.ts`, with tests in `fs.test.ts`. > > - **Behavior**: > - `readDirectory()` in `fs.ts` now resolves symlinks using `fs.readlink()` and inspects target stats. > - Supports symlinks to files and directories, recursively traversing symlinked directories. > - Safely ignores circular symlinks to prevent infinite loops. > - **Tests**: > - Added unit tests in `fs.test.ts` for symlink handling, including symlink to file, symlink to directory, and error handling for non-existent directories. > - **Misc**: > - Added a changeset `soft-windows-melt.md` describing the bug fix. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=cline%2Fcline&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for 13ce4b76a7317a5f78df6d001b8d155b70a1c490.
